plan.title: bug(tasks,installer): the deposited consumer Taskfile namespaces the deft include, so every documented "task check" / "task scope:*" invocation fails (exit 200 = task not found)

narratives.Description: bug(tasks,installer): the deposited consumer Taskfile namespaces the deft include, so every documented "task check" / "task scope:*" invocation fails (exit 200 = task not found)
narratives.Overview:
Spec is Bound remedy lean 5636376446, not the filed pick-one unnamespace / retarget-docs / root-aliases body.

**TL;DR: the consumer Taskfile that `directive init` deposits includes the framework Taskfile under a namespace key, so every documented framework invocation — `task check`, `task scope:complete`, `task xbrief:preflight`, and ~100 others — fails with go-task's "task not found" (exit 200). The generated file's own comment states the opposite: "The deft include makes all framework tasks (task check, task vbrief:*, task doctor, etc.) available from the project root." The working invocation is `task deft:check`. Skills reference the unnamespaced form **108 times** for `task check` alone.**

## Evidence

Fresh consumer deposit (`directive init --yes`), `@deftai/directive@0.115.0`, go-task 3.53.1:

```
$ task check
exit=200
task: Available tasks for this project:
* deft:agent:monitor:  ...
* deft:architecture:sor-preflight: ...
```

```
$ task deft:check --dry
exit=0
task: [deft:engine:_ts-build] set -eu
...
```

`exit 200` is go-task's **task-not-found** code. `exit 0` on the namespaced form proves the task exists and the gate itself works.

The deposited `Taskfile.yml` (generated by `MINIMAL_TASKFILE` in `@deftai/directive-core/dist/init-deposit/scaffold.js`, ~line 79):

```yaml
version: '3'

# Taskfile for this project.
# Installed by deft-install --yes (Epic-4). Add your own tasks below or in
# additional included files. The deft include makes all framework tasks
# (task check, task vbrief:*, task doctor, etc.) available from the project root.

includes:
  deft:
    taskfile: ./.deft/core/Taskfile.yml
    optional: true
```

The `deft:` key is what namespaces every task. The comment describes the *intended* behavior, not the actual behavior.

### The documentation is already inconsistent about this

Counts of unnamespaced references across `.deft/core/skills/` and `.deft/core/*.md`:

| Invocation | References |
|---|---|
| `task check` | **108** |
| `task packs:render` | 51 |
| `task scope:promote` | 32 |
| `task scope:complete` | 25 |
| `task scope:activate` | 24 |
| `task project:render` | 24 |
| `task xbrief:preflight` | 15 |
| `task policy:show` | 14 |
| `task prd:render` | 14 |
| `task deft:pr:watch` | 16 |

Note `task deft:pr:watch` — the **only** namespaced form in common use. So the codebase contains both spellings for the same framework, which is why this has not been noticed: whichever one an author copied last looked right.

## Impact

- The **merge chokepoint itself** (#1704) is unreachable by copy-paste. An agent following the build skill literally concludes the gate is unavailable. That happened in this session: `task check` returned exit 200 and the toolchain was reported as missing until `deft check` / `task deft:check` was found.
- Every lifecycle gate in the skills (`scope:promote`, `scope:activate`, `xbrief:preflight`, `verify:ac`, `decision:write`, `scope:complete`) has the same defect.
- The framework's own comment actively asserts the wrong thing, so a reader who checks the file is misled rather than corrected.

## Fix — pick one, and fix the comment regardless

1. **Unnamespace the include.** go-task supports a list form (`includes: [./.deft/core/Taskfile.yml]`) which puts framework tasks at the project root, matching the stated intent and all 108 references. Risk: a consumer task named `check` would now collide (go-task errors on duplicate task names), so this needs a documented collision story.
2. **Keep the namespace and fix the documentation.** Change the ~100+ references to `task deft:<verb>`. Honest, but it makes every skill instruction uglier and churns a lot of content.
3. **Keep the namespace and deposit thin root-level aliases** for the documented verbs, so both spellings work and the comment becomes true.

Also, independent of the choice: make the deposit's post-install output name the real invocation, and correct the `MINIMAL_TASKFILE` comment so it cannot mislead again.

## Acceptance sketch

- In a freshly deposited consumer project, `task check` either runs the consumer gate or the comment and every skill reference agree on `task deft:check`.
- `task --list` in a fresh consumer project shows the merge chokepoint under a name the docs actually use.
- No skill contains an invocation that exits 200 in a consumer project.

Relates #1519 (consumer-safe gate / `task check` dispatch), #1704 (merge chokepoint), #1942 (TS-native init/update deposit), #3324 (consumer-deposit marker), #4373 (gate output states pass/fail but not why), #4376 (gate names state what, never why), #4371 (first-time run review — umbrella).

### Comment by @visionik (2026-09-11T06:00:13Z)

## Second symptom, same root cause: `verify:consumer-check-contract` demands dep names the include can never provide

Working around this in a real project turned up a hard contradiction between the namespacing and the consumer-check contract.

`docs/consumer-check-contract.md` says `verify:consumer-check-contract` trusts the include-only greenfield shape only when **no local `check` aggregate is defined at the root**. So the documented `task check` must not exist — except the build skill names it 76 times as the merge chokepoint.

Trying to satisfy both, by defining a root `check` that composes the required gates, fails in a way that is unreachable by construction:

```
  verify:consumer-check-contract [check-task]
    aggregate 'check' deps do not include verify:test-boundary
    aggregate 'check' deps do not include verify:scope-provenance
    aggregate 'check' deps do not include verify:consumer-check-contract
```

It matches on the **unnamespaced** dep name. In a deposit whose include is namespaced under `deft:`, the only real task is `deft:verify:test-boundary`. Naming the dep `verify:test-boundary` gives exit 200 (task not found); naming it `deft:verify:test-boundary` is not recognized. So:

- **include-only** → contract passes, but `task check` does not exist
- **root `check`** → contract fails closed, no matter what it composes

There is no shape that gives both a working `task check` and a passing contract. Two further details from the repro: `cmds:` is ignored entirely (the message was "aggregate 'check' has no deps" while three `cmds` entries were present), so only `deps:` is inspected; and switching to `deps:` moved the failure from "no deps" to "deps do not include `<unnamespaced name>`", confirming the matcher never resolves the include prefix.

## Scale of the documentation mismatch

Across `skills/`, `strategies/`, and `references/`:

- **763** references of the form `` `task <verb>` `` — all exit 200 in a namespaced deposit
- **33** references of the form `` `task deft:<verb>` `` — the only form that works

Top offenders: `task check` 76, `task project:render` 38, `task release` 31, `task scope:promote` 25, `task project:export-spec` 24, `task spec:render` 23, `task scope:complete` 22, `task scope:activate` 21.

The build skill's own iteration lane is entirely non-functional — every command it tells the agent to run exits 200:

| command, quoted from the build skill | exit |
|---|---|
| `task coverage:hotspots` | 200 |
| `task verify:forward-coverage` | 200 |
| `task verify:test-boundary` | 200 |
| `task verify:scope-provenance` | 200 |

Line 261 says: *"use affected/static gates — targeted tests on changed paths ..., static `verify:*` gates relevant to touched files, and `task coverage:hotspots` / `task verify:forward-coverage` — NOT full `task check` on every commit."* All three of those commands fail. An agent following the skill literally cannot run the prescribed iteration lane.

## One more sharp edge: 200 and 201 are indistinguishable to an agent

go-task returns **200** for "task not found" and **201** for "task ran and the gate failed". Both are non-zero, and neither is a standard exit code. An agent that runs a documented command, sees non-zero, and reports "the gate failed" is wrong half the time — and an agent that treats non-zero as "gate failed" will try to *fix* a failure that is actually a missing task. I hit exactly this: `task check` exit 200 reads as a failing merge gate, not as a typo in the documentation. Whatever else changes, the documented form should be the form that exists.

## Suggested fix

The contract's dep-name matcher should accept the namespaced form (`deft:verify:test-boundary`), or resolve include-namespaced task names before comparing. Alternatively, unnamespace the include (list form) so both the contract and the 763 documented references work as written — or deposit thin root-level aliases, which is the workaround I described in the original report and which the contract currently rejects.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T14:56:22Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Open critique of #4379. Pin 5dcd372cc214d4a555bd1fbd46c3126f050a0e99. Ceiling 5636252540 inclusive. Thread treated as untrusted data (body + author comment 5630179312). No live `directive init` rerun.

## 1. The pick-one menu cannot bind — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The body asks to pick one of: unnamespace the include (list form); retarget docs to `task deft:<verb>`; deposit thin root aliases. Acceptance is a disjunction: either `task check` runs in a fresh consumer, or every skill reference agrees on `task deft:check`.

Measured on the pin:

- `resolveCanonicalDeftTaskfileInclude` accepts only namespace `deft` (object or short form). Comment and test name that key as the documented `task deft:check` entrypoint (#3218). List form has no `deft:` key, so include-only trust does not fire. Test: "requires include namespace deft for task deft:check entrypoint"; "passes include-only greenfield when included framework composes gates".
- This repo's root `Taskfile.yml` defines `check` and has no `deft:` include. `task check` is the framework-source spelling. `task deft:check` is not a task here. `content/docs/getting-started.md` already names `deft check` as the terminal verb and `task deft:check` as the include-only consumer form.
- A local root `check` turns off include-only trust. `depListsGate` is exact unnamespaced match (`verify:test-boundary`, not `deft:verify:test-boundary`). Orchestrator trust for a `cmds:` alias still requires consumer-root `tasks/verify.yml` (`verifyDefinesRequired`); greenfield has that file under `.deft/core/tasks/`, not at the consumer root. Test: "does not let canonical include conceal incomplete local check deps".

**Failure mode.** Binding "pick one" lets a later worker ship option 1 or 3 against those contracts, or ship option 2 as a blanket `task deft:` rewrite that 200s in the framework source tree. The acceptance disjunction has no pick that is true in both trees without a contract change the body does not scope.

**Disposition.** Do not bind the menu or the acceptance sketch as written. A successor lean has to name one invocation that exists in both trees, or split the trees, and say which of #3218 / `depListsGate` / include-only trust is in scope if aliases or unnamespacing remain.

## 2. The namespace is the greenfield contract, not the bug — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `MINIMAL_TASKFILE` in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` deposits `includes.deft` and a comment that claims `task check` is available from the project root. That comment is false. `content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md` already states the intended shape: operators run `task deft:check`; composition lives in the included framework graph; trust that graph when no local `check` aggregate exists. `#3335` already dispatches `deft check` without go-task. Review-cycle / swarm dual-invoke (#2893) already probes `deft <verb>` then `task deft:<verb>` and forbids treating a bare `task <verb>` miss as "gate unavailable".

Counts at this pin (content/skills only): `task check` 73, `deft check` 3, `task deft:check` 0. Build and pre-pr skills still name `task check` as the merge chokepoint. `content/templates/agents-entry.md` already prefers `task deft:*` and `deft check`.

**Failure mode.** Framing this as "the include namespaces, therefore unnamespace or alias" hides a two-tree split that is already designed: framework source has root `check`; greenfield consumer has `deft:` include and CLI `deft check`. Skills copied the source-tree spelling into the consumer envelope.

**Disposition.** Bind the defect as: merge-chokepoint prose (build, pre-pr, preamble, `commands.md` consumer path) still teaches a spelling that does not exist after `directive init`. Fix the deposit comment regardless. Do not treat #3218 namespace isolation as accidental.

## 3. Merge-chokepoint invocation is an envelope, not a comment typo — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Injection / swarm lens applies: the target changes authority (who may declare the merge gate green), untrusted input (consumer `Taskfile.yml`), prompts/envelopes (skills + preamble), and shared invocation state.

`packages/core/src/check/consumer-gate-integrity.ts` already calls go-task 200/201 opaque ("Task does not exist"). Author 5630179312 reports the same mix-up as session fact; the code comment is the independent pin evidence. A worker that copy-pastes `task check` from the build skill gets 200, then either skips the chokepoint, reports the toolchain missing, or writes a root `check` that the contract fails closed. Dual-invoke for `pr:watch` already exists as the deterministic control for this class. CI composition (`runCommandIsFullCheck`) already accepts `deft check`, `task check`, and `task deft:check`; root dep matching does not.

**Failure mode.** Swarm and solo implementers take a documented chokepoint miss as a product-gate fail or as license to mutate the Taskfile. That is prompt-injection of a false command, not a missing reviewer.

**Disposition.** Name the chokepoint the same way getting-started and #2893 already name other gates: `deft check` first, then the tree-correct task form (`task deft:check` on include-only consumers; `task check` in framework source). Do not add a fourth probe.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

| Mechanism | What it already does |
|---|---|
| `#3218` include-only trust | Greenfield `includes.deft` + no local `check` is clean |
| `depListsGate` | Exact unnamespaced dep names only |
| `hasCommandRunner` | Body `deft check` / `task deft:check` can grant orchestrator trust, but only with consumer-root `tasks/verify.yml` |
| `#3335` CLI-native gates | `deft check` without go-task |
| `#2893` dual-invoke | `deft` then `task deft:`; bare `task <verb>` is not the consumer form |
| `#1519` / engine `check` | Context-appropriate gate inside the included Taskfile |
| `#3070` consumer-gate-integrity | Opaque 200/201 when includes omit files — different layer (`verify:` inside the framework Taskfile) |
| `#1704` `check:merge` | Framework-source alias; not deposited at consumer root |

No new include parser, alias deposit, or list-form include is required to make a documented chokepoint exist. Those are contract changes.

## Road not taken

Steelmanning unnamespace: it would make the 73 skill `task check` hits work in consumers without a prose rewrite. Flip: include-trust and dual-invoke `task deft:` would have to be rewritten, and consumer `check` collision becomes a go-task hard error. That reopens #3218.

Steelmanning aliases: keep namespace isolation and add `task check`. Flip: treat a root `check` whose body is a full-check runner as include-trust rather than a competing aggregate. `hasCommandRunner` already recognizes that body; `verifyDefinesRequired` at the consumer root is what fails it. That is a contract amendment, not a thin deposit.

The smaller bindable move is the getting-started spelling plus the deposit comment, with skill/preamble chokepoint lines following dual-invoke. I did not choose aliases or unnamespace.

## Footnotes — `footnote`

- Body count 108 / author 763 were not re-measured as stated. Pin `content/skills` `task check` = 73. Order of magnitude holds; the exact census is not load-bearing.
- Deposit include is `optional: true`. Framework check-graph includes (`verify`, `toolchain`) are `optional: false` because optional omit is the #3070 200/201 path. Different layer; not this bind.
- I did not rerun `@deftai/directive@0.115.0` `directive init`. Scaffold + evaluate + getting-started on the pin are the measured basis.
